## 3rd-Party App Governance API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/3rd-party-app-governance-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > 3rd-Party App Governance API

3rd-Party App Governance API

**Constraints:**

- For query parameters, ensure that the provided characters adhere to the specifications outlined in RFC 7230 and RFC 3986.
- Special characters and encoding must follow the standards defined in RFC 3986.

**Servers:** `https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1`

### `GET /apps/app`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/apps/app

**Constraints:**

- For query parameters, ensure that the provided characters adhere to the specifications outlined in RFC 7230 and RFC 3986.
- Special characters and encoding must follow the standards defined in RFC 3986.

Searches the 3rd-Party App Governance App Catalog by either app ID or URL (i.e., a valid consent or marketplace link). You must use one of the required parameters—

`app_id`

or

`url`

—for your search. If you use both an app ID and a URL for your search, an error is returned.

- If the app is found in the catalog, a `200` response is received and the app's information is returned.
- If the app is not initially found in the catalog, a `202` response is received and the app is submitted for analysis in the 3rd-Party App Governance Sandbox.

- If the app is not found in the catalog, a `404` response is received.
- If the URL is not valid, a `400` response is received.

To learn more, see the Responses in the right-side panel.

- Operation ID: `getApp`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | query | no | string | The app identifier (e.g., OAuth client ID) |
| `url` | query | no | string | Valid consent link or marketplace link |
| `verbose` | query | no | boolean | Return a verbose report including potentially heavy artifacts (e.g., extracted URLs and a list of vulnerabilities) |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 202 | Application Analysis Underway |
| 400 | Bad Input Parameter |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 404 | Application Not Found |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | Internal Server Error Occurred |

### `POST /apps/app`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/apps/app

Submits an app for analysis in the 3rd-Party App Governance Sandbox. After analysis is complete, a subsequent

`GET`

request is required to fetch the app's information.

- Operation ID: `postApp`

**Request body:** `application/json` → SimpleAppIdRequest

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 400 | Invalid Request Body |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | Internal Server Error Occurred |

### `GET /apps/search`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/apps/search

**Constraints:**

- For query parameters, ensure that the provided characters adhere to the specifications outlined in RFC 7230 and RFC 3986.
- Special characters and encoding must follow the standards defined in RFC 3986.

Searches for an app by name. Any app whose name contains the search term (

`appName`

) is returned.

**Note**

: The maximum number of results that are returned is 200.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appName` | query | yes | string | The app name |
| `limit` | query | no | integer | Limit the number of results |
| `page` | query | no | integer | Page number |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 400 | Invalid Request Body |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | Internal Server Error Occurred |

### `GET /app_views/{appViewId}/accounts`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/app_views/{appViewId}/accounts

Retrieves the associated user accounts for a view ID. This endpoint accepts a view ID and returns a map. Each key in the map is an app ID.

- For app instances authorized by individual users, the value is an array of strings containing those users' email addresses.
- For app instances that are authorized for the entire tenant, the value is `null`.
- If an app instance has no users, the value is an empty array.

- Operation ID: `getAppIdsToAccounts`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `` |  | no | object |  |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Success. Returns a map where keys are app IDs and values are a list of associated user emails. The value is `null` if the app is authorized for the entire tenant. |
| 400 | Invalid Request Body. The list of app instance IDs in the request body cannot be empty. |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | An internal server error occurred |

### `GET /app_views/list`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/app_views/list

- Operation ID: `getViews`

**Responses:**

| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 400 | Invalid Request Body |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | Internal Server Error Occurred |

### `GET /app_views/{appViewId}/apps`

https://api.apptotal.zscaler.com/v1/app_views/{appViewId}/apps

Retrieves all assets (i.e., apps) that are related to a specified argument (i.e.,

[custom view](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/custom-views\)

). Uses the value of

`id`

from

`GET /app_views/list`

to return the app IDs of the apps related to the custom view.

- Operation ID: `getViewApps`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appViewId` | path | yes | string | The custom view identifier |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 400 | Invalid Request Body |
| 401 | Not Authenticated |
| 403 | Access Forbidden |
| 409 | Rate Limit Exceeded |
| 500 | Internal Server Error Occurred |

## Understanding Error Codes

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/about-error-codes
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Zscaler Client Connector API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Understanding Error Codes
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: Information on HTTP status codes for Zscaler Client Connector API.

The following table lists the HTTP status codes returned by the Zscaler Client Connector API:

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 429 | Too Many Requests The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time and exceeded the rate limit or device threshold. To learn more, see [Understanding Rate Limiting](https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/understanding-rate-limiting). |
| 500 | Not Implemented |

## Activation

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/activation
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Activation
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /eusaStatus/latest`

Retrieves the End User Subscription Agreement (EUSA) acceptance status. If the status does not exist, it returns a status object with no ID.

- Operation ID: `EusaStatusZResource_getEusaStatusForLatestEusaInfoId`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `PUT /eusaStatus/{eusaStatusId}`

Updates the EUSA status based on the specified status ID

- Operation ID: `EusaStatusZResource_updateEusaStatus`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eusaStatusId` | path | yes | object | The EUSA status ID |
| `body` | body | no | EusaStatus | The EUSA status details |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /status`

Gets the activation status for the saved configuration changes. To learn more about activating configuration changes, see [Saving and Activating Changes in the ZIA Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/saving-and-activating-changes-zia-admin-portal).

- Operation ID: `getOrganizationActivationStatus`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /status/activate`

Activates the saved configuration changes. To learn more, see [Saving and Activating Changes in the ZIA Admin Portal](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/saving-and-activating-changes-zia-admin-portal).

- Operation ID: `activateOrganizationalChanges`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

## Admin Audit Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/admin-audit-logs
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Admin Audit Logs
- Last modified: 2026-04-27T07:06Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /auditlogEntryReport`

Retrieves the audit log report generation status based on the specified report status ID (retrieved from POST `/auditlogEntryReport` response). You need to continue polling for the report status until a terminal status is reached (e.g., `COMPLETE`) to download the report subsequently.

To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `getAuditReportEntryCsvExportStatus`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /auditlogEntryReport`

Generates an audit log report for the specified time period. The report includes audit information for every call made to the cloud service API during the specified time period. Creating a new audit log report overwrites a previously generated report.

After making this POST request, you need to poll for the report status by sending GET requests to `/auditlogEntryReport` along with the status ID obtained from the POST request. Continue polling until the report reaches a terminal status (e.g., `COMPLETE` or `CANCELLED`). When the status is `COMPLETE`, you can download the report as a CSV file by sending a GET request to `/auditlogEntryReport/download`. To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `startAuditReportEntryCsvExport`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | body | no | AuditLogEntryRequest | Criteria used for generating the audit log report, such as time range, filters, pagination, etc. To learn more, see [About Audit Logs](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-audit-logs). |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `DELETE /auditlogEntryReport`

Cancels the request previously made to create an audit log report

- Operation ID: `cancelAuditReportEntryCsvExport`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /auditlogEntryReport/download`

Downloads the most recently created audit log report based on the specified report status ID.

Before sending this request, ensure that you generate a report using `POST /auditlogEntryReport` and poll for report status using `GET /auditlogEntryReport` until the status indicates the report is completed (i.e., status is `COMPLETE`). To learn more, see [Downloading Audit Logs and Event Logs Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/downloading-audit-logs-event-logs-using-api).

- Operation ID: `getAuditReportEntryCsvData`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statusId` | query | yes | object | The status ID for the report obtained from the response of the POST /auditlogEntryReport request that was used to create the report |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

For example, this field must be set to true when creating an admin user in ZIA who's already a user in Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX). To learn more, see [Adding ZIA Admins](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-zia-admins). |

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `DELETE /adminUsers/{userId}`

Deletes an admin or auditor user using the specified ID

**Note**: This request deletes an admin and removes them as a user from the ZIA Admin Portal. To delete the admin privileges for a user while retaining them as a regular user of your organization in the ZIA Admin Portal, use the `POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser` request.

**Sample Request (Python)**

```
import http.client
import json
conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("HOSTNAME")
headers = {
'content-type': "application/json",
'cache-control': "no-cache",
'cookie': "JSESSIONID=xxxxxxx"
}
conn.request("DELETE", "/api/v1/adminUsers/6794036", headers=headers)
res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()
print(data.decode("utf-8"))
```

**Sample Response**

```
204 No Content
```

- Operation ID: `deleteAdminUser`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userId` | path | yes | object | The unique identifier for the admin/auditor user. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 204 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /adminUsers/me`

Retrieves information about the current administrator or auditor user, or both

- Operation ID: `AdminUserZResource_getCurrentUser`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser`

Removes admin privileges for a user while retaining them as a regular user of your organization in the ZIA Admin Portal. This can be used as an alternative to the `DELETE /adminUsers/{userId}` request, which deletes an admin and removes them as a user from the ZIA Admin Portal. To learn more, see [Deleting ZIA Admins](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/deleting-zia-admins).

Before you can delete the admin privileges for a user, you need to obtain the admin user's ID and other information by using the `GET /users` request and then send the admin user details in the `POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser` request.

- Operation ID: `AdminUserResource_convertAdminToEndUser`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userId` | path | yes | object | The unique identifier of the admin user |
| `body` | body | no | User | Information about the user for whom the admin privileges must be removed. Group information is mandatory in the request Body. Optionally, you can include other field information to modify the values. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

## Alerts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/alerts-zdx-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZDX API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Alerts

APIs for Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX).

**Servers:** `https://api.zdxcloud.net/v1`, `https://dev.zdxapi.zscaler.net/v1`, `http://localhost:8080/v1`

### `GET /alerts/ongoing`

Gets the list of ongoing alert rules across an organization. All ongoing alert rules are returned if the search filter is not specified. The endpoint defaults to the previous 2 hours. Ongoing alerts are alerts that don't have an Ended On date. The alert rule's Started On date is used in conjunction with the provided filters. Cannot exceed the 14-day time range limit for alert rules.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 401 |  |
| 403 |  |

### `GET /alerts/historical`

Gets the list of alert history rules defined across an organization. All alert history rules are returned if the search filter is not specified. The default is set to the previous 2 hours. Alert history rules have an Ended On date. The Ended On date is used to pull alerts in conjunction with the provided filters. Cannot exceed the 14-day time range limit for alert rules.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 401 |  |
| 403 |  |

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alert_id` | path | yes | string |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |
| `` |  | no | object |  |

## API Authentication

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-authentication

- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > API Authentication
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /authenticatedSession`

Checks if there is an authentication session.

- Operation ID: `getAuthenticatedSession`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation. When an authenticated session exists, the response contains authType information. If authType is not present, the authenticated session has expired or it does not exist. |
| 503 | Service is temporarily unavailable due to maintenance |

### `POST /authenticatedSession`

Creates an authenticated session. The response returns a cookie in the header called `JSESSIONID` that must be used in subsequent requests.

- Operation ID: `postAuthenticatedSessionInfo`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `credentials` | body | yes | AuthCredentials | User credential. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation. The response contains authType information only when authentication has completed successfully, regardless of the response code given. |

### `DELETE /authenticatedSession`

Ends an authenticated session.

- Operation ID: `setAuthenticatedSessionInfo`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## API Clients

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-clients
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Authentication Service API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > API Clients
- Last modified: 2026-07-27T07:06Z

**Servers:** `https://api.zsapi.net/ziam/admin/api/v1`

### `GET /api-clients`

Retrieves a paginated list of API clients, providing details such as total records, current page offset, and links for pagination navigation. To learn more, see

[About API Clients](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/about-api-clients)

.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_list`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | query | no | integer(int32) | The starting point for pagination, with the number of records that can be skipped before fetching results. |
| `limit` | query | no | integer(int32) | The maximum number of records to return per request. Minimum: `0`, Maximum: `1000` |
| `` |  | no | object |  |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The request was successful, and a paginated list of API clients is returned. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

### `POST /api-clients`

Creates a new API client with authentication settings and assigned roles.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_add`

**Request body:** `application/json` → object

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result. |
| 202 | The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed. |
| 400 | The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax. |

### `PUT /api-clients/{id}`

Updates the existing API client details based on the provided

`ID`

. This allows modification of attributes such as name, authentication settings, and assigned roles.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_update`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the API client to be updated. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → object

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The request was successful, and the API client details are updated. |
| 500 | Unexpected server issue occurred while processing the request. |

### `DELETE /api-clients/{id}`

Removes an existing API client from the system. After deletion, the API client cannot be recovered.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_remove`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the API client to be deleted. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 204 | The API client was successfully deleted. No content is returned in the response, but headers may be useful for validation purposes. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

### `GET /api-clients/{id}`

Retrieves detailed information about a specific API client using its

`ID`

.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_get`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the API client to be retrieved. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The request was successful, and the API client details are returned. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

### `GET /api-clients/{id}/secrets`

Retrieves a list of secrets associated with a specific API client using its `ID`.

**NOTE:**

- Secret values in the response are masked to prevent exposure of sensitive information.
- This API is applicable only when the authentication type is **SECRET**.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_getSecrets`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | The API client `ID` to retrieve the client secrets. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | The request was successful, and a list of secrets is returned. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

### `POST /api-clients/{id}/secrets`

Creates and associates a new secret with a specified API client `ID`. This secret can be used for authentication with Authentication Service.

**NOTE:** This API is applicable only when the authentication type is **SECRET**.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_addSecret`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the API client to which the secret is added. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → ClientSecretReqDto

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 201 | The request was successful, and a new secret has been created and associated with the API client. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

### `DELETE /api-clients/{id}/secrets/{secretsId}`

Removes a specific secret associated with an API client using the Client ID and secret ID. After deletion, the secret cannot be recovered.

- Operation ID: `ApiclientOps_deleteSecret`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the API client. |
| `secretsId` | path | yes | string | Unique identifier of the secret to be deleted. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 204 | The secret was successfully deleted. No content is returned in the response, but may be useful for validation purposes. |
| 401 | Authentication failed or missing authorization credentials. The request requires a valid Bearer Token. However, either no token was provided, or the provided token is invalid or expired. |

## API Key Management

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-key-management-zpa-api-reference
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > API Key Management
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z

To access detailed ZPA API documentation, including references and use cases, refer to the [Zscaler Help Portal](/zpa/about-zpa-api).

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/apiKeys`

**Gets details of all API keys for the specified customer.**

- Operation ID: `getClientCredentials`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The ZPA tenant ID of the customer. |
| `page` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page number. |
| `pagesize` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The maximum page size is 500. |
| `search` | query | no | string | The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API. |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API Keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 200 | OK |

## API Response Codes and Error Messages

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > API Response Codes and Error Messages
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: Information on HTTP status codes for Zscaler's cloud service API.

The following HTTP status codes are returned by the API:

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful |
| 204 | Successful. No content returned. |
| 400 | Invalid or bad request |
| 401 | Session is not authenticated or timed out |
| 403 | This code is returned due to one of the following reasons: The API key was disabled by your service provider; User's role has no access permissions or functional scope; A required SKU subscription is missing; API operations that use POST, PUT, or DELETE methods are performed when the ZIA Admin Portal is in maintenance mode during a scheduled upgradeContact Zscaler Support or your Zscaler Account team for assistance. |
| 404 | Resource does not exist |
| 405 | Method not allowed. This error is returned when the request method is not supported by the target resource. |
| 409 | Request could not be processed because of possible edit conflict occurred. Another admin might be saving a configuration change at the same time. In this scenario, the client is expected to retry after a short time period. |
| 415 | Unsupported media type. This error is returned if you don't include `application/json` as the `Content-Type` in the request header (for example, `Content-Type: application/json`). |
| 429 | Exceeded the rate limit or quota. The response includes a `Retry-After` value. |
| 500 | Unexpected error |
| 503 | Service is temporarily unavailable |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages-1","lastmod":"2026-01-06T23:49Z","nid":"1484801"} -->
## API Response Codes and Error Messages

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages-1
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > API Response Codes and Error Messages
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: Information about the Zscaler Private Access public API error codes.

The following table lists the HTTP status codes returned by the API.

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful |
| 201 | Created |
| 204 | No Content |
| 400 | Bad Request For example: { "id": "resource.not.found", "reason": "No resource exists with the given id/name :0", "params": [ "0" ] } |
| 401 | Unauthorized For example: { id: “access.denied”, reason: “Access denied” } |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 409 | Conflict For example: `{ "params":[ "com.zscaler.zpn.model.PolicySet" ], "id":"api.concurrent.access.error", "reason":"Unable to modify the resource due to concurrent change requests. Try again" }`Concurrent API calls using POST, PUT, and DELETE methods to the policy set controller might return error 409 - Conflict. Ensure that only one PUT request per policy rule is sent at a given time. |
| 429 | Exceeded the rate limit or quota The following example is the response body when an API call is rate limited: `{ "exception": "invalid.toomanyrequests", "id": "invalid.toomanyrequests", "reason": "Exceeded the number of requests allowed" }`The following example is the response header when an API call is rate limited: `{ "content-type": "application/json", "date": "Wed, 6 Mar 2024 11:38 GMT", "retry-after": "13s" }`To learn more, see [Understanding Rate Limiting](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-rate-limiting). |
| 503 | Service Unavailable The following example is a response body for error code 503: `{ "id": "retryable.server.error", "reason": "An error occurred. Refer to the Retry-After header, and then try again." }`The following is an example response header: `{Retry-After: 10s}` Zscaler recommends an exponential backoff strategy before retrying. If a `Retry-After` header is available as part of the response headers, wait until the stipulated time mentioned in the `Retry-After` header before retrying. |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

---

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages-2","lastmod":"2026-01-20T01:28Z","nid":"1447246"} -->
## API Response Codes and Error Messages

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages-2
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector API > API Developer & Reference Guide > API Response Codes and Error Messages
- Last modified: 2026-01-20T01:28Z
- Summary: Information about error codes in the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector API

The following HTTP status codes are returned by the API:

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 OK | Successful |
| 201 Created | New resource was successfully created. |
| 204 No Content | Successful. No content returned. |
| 400 Bad Request | Request not completed due to incorrect syntax. |
| 401 Unauthorized | Session is not authenticated or timed out. |
| 403 Forbidden | This code is returned for one of the following reasons: The API key was disabled by your service provider.; User's role has no access permissions or functional scope.; API operations that use POST, PUT, or DELETE methods were performed when the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal is in maintenance mode during a scheduled upgrade.Contact Zscaler Support or your Zscaler Account team for assistance. |
| 404 Not Found | Resource does not exist. |
| 409 Conflict | Request could not be processed because a possible edit conflict occurred. Another admin might be saving configuration changes at the same time. In this scenario, the client is expected to retry after a short time period. |
| 415 Unsupported Media Type | Unsupported media type. This error is returned if you don't include `application/json` as the `Content-Type` in the request header (for example, `Content-Type: application/json`). |
| 429 Too Many Requests | Exceeded the rate limit or quota. The response includes a `Retry-After` value. |
| 500 Internal Server Error | Unexpected error. |
| 503 Service Unavailable | Service is temporarily unavailable. |

## API Response Codes and Error Messages

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/api-response-codes-and-error-messages-4
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Authentication Service API > API Developer & Reference Guide > API Response Codes and Error Messages
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z
- Summary: Information about the Authentication Service public API error codes.

The following table outlines the HTTP status codes returned by the API.

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK - The request was successful, and the server returned the expected response. |
| 201 | Created - new resource was successfully created. |
| 202 | Accepted - The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet been completed. |
| 204 | No Content - The request was processed successfully, but no content is returned in the response. |
| 400 | Bad Request - The request contains invalid syntax or parameters. |
| 401 | Unauthorized - Authentication is required or provided credentials are incorrect. |
| 403 | Forbidden - Indicates that the server understood the request but did not process it. |
| 404 | Not Found - The requested resource was not found on the server. |
| 406 | Not Acceptable - The server could not provide a response that matches the content type requested by the client. |
| 409 | Conflict - The server encountered a request that conflicts with the current state of the resource. |
| 413 | Payload Too Large - The server cannot process the request because the request's payload exceeds the server's configured limit. |
| 500 | Internal Server Error - An unexpected server issue occurred, preventing the request from being processed. |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## App Connector Group Management

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/app-connector-group-management
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > App Connector Group Management
- Last modified: 2026-07-30T16:29Z

To access detailed ZPA API documentation, including references and use cases, refer to the [Zscaler Help Portal](/zpa/about-zpa-api).

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/appConnectorGroup/{appConnectorGroupId}/sg`

Gets App Connector group and server group details for the specified customer.

- Operation ID: `getAssistantGroupWithSG_1`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `appConnectorGroupId` | path | yes | integer(int64) |  |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API Keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |

Gets the App Connector group details for the specified ID.

- Operation ID: `getAssistantGroup_2`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `appConnectorGroupId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the App Connector group. |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API Keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. Access to certain operations is limited when you are within a Microtenant. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |

| 401 | Unauthorized |

### `PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/appConnectorGroup/{appConnectorGroupId}`

Updates the App Connector group details for the specified ID.

- Operation ID: `updateAssistantGroup_1`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `appConnectorGroupId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the App Connector group. |
| `microtenantId` | query | no | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. If you are within a Microtenant, you must pass the microtenantId field when making an API call to retrieve data from that Microtenant. The microtenantId can be obtained from the API Keys page, or can be obtained programmatically using the ZPA cloud service API. If you are within the Default Microtenant, pass microtenantId as 0 when making requests to retrieve data from the Default Microtenant. If the microtenantId is not passed in the request when creating or updating a resource, then the resource is created or updated in the Default Microtenant. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → AppConnectorGroup

**Responses:**

| 400 | Bad Request |

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/getDefaultInspectionProfile`

Gets the default AppProtection profile for the specified customer.

- Operation ID: `getDefaultInspectionProfile`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |

### `PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/inspectionProfile/{inspectionProfileId}/dissociateAllPredefinedControls`

Updates the AppProtection profile for the specified ID and dissociates all predefined controls from a profile.

- Operation ID: `dissociateAllPredefinedControls`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `inspectionProfileId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the AppProtection profile. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |

| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |

API Reference Guide for the Zscaler EASM API

### `GET /organizations/:orgId/assets`

Retrieves the list of internet-facing assets that EASM detects for your organization. To learn more, see

[About Asset Inventory](https://help.zscaler.com/easm/about-asset-inventory)

and

[Understanding Asset Discovery](https://help.zscaler.com/easm/understanding-asset-discovery)

.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | yes | object | API authentication token |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

### `GET /organizations/:orgId/assets/:assetId/certificates`

Retrieves the list of SSL/TLS certificates used on an asset based on the specified asset ID. To learn more, see

[Understanding Asset Details](https://help.zscaler.com/easm/understanding-asset-details)

.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | yes | object | API authentication token |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

### `GET /organizations/:orgId/assets/:assetId/services`

Retrieves the list of services running on an asset based on the specified asset ID. To learn more, see

[Understanding Asset Details](https://help.zscaler.com/easm/understanding-asset-details)

.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | yes | object | API authentication token |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

### `GET /organizations/:orgId/assets/:assetId/technologies`

Retrieves the list of technologies used on an asset based on the specified asset ID. To learn more, see

[Understanding Asset Details](https://help.zscaler.com/easm/understanding-asset-details)

.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | header | yes | object | API authentication token |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

## Audit Logs

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/audit-logs
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > Workflow Automation API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Audit Logs
- Last modified: 2026-01-06T23:49Z

Zscaler Workflow Automation - DLP Incident Management API.

**Servers:** `https://api.us1.zsworkflow.net`

### `POST /dlp/v1/customer/audit`

Filters audit logs based on the specified time period and field values. The result includes audit information for every action made by the admins in the Workflow Automation Admin Portal and the actions made through APIs. The supported field values are:

- Action
- Resource
- Admin
- Module

The supported time range values are:

- Start date and time
- End date and time

- Operation ID: `searchAuditLogs`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | query | no | integer | Specifies the page number of the incident in a multi-paginated response. This field is not required if page ID field is used. |
| `pageSize` | query | no | integer | Specifies the page size (i.e., number of incidents per page). |
| `pageId` | query | no | string | Specifies the page ID of the incident in a multi-paginated response. It is a unique identifier returned in the first search request. The page ID can be used instead of the page number in subsequent search requests for faster and more efficient results. |

**Request body:** `application/json` → SearchRequestFilters

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful operation |
| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Authorization failure |
| 500 | Failed to process the request |

### Schemas

**`SearchRequestFilters`**

| Property | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | array<ZSDLPIncidentSearchFieldValue> | no |
| `timeRange` | ZSDLPIncidentSearchTimeRange | no |

**`ZSAuditLogResponseList`**

| Property | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | Cursor | no |
| `logs` | array<ZSAuditLogResponse> | no |

**`ZSDLPIncidentSearchFieldValue`**

| Property | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | ZSDLPIncidentSearchableFields | no |
| `value` | array<string> | no |

- `ZSDLPIncidentSearchableFields`: string (enum: severity, priority, transactionId, status, source, sourceDLPType, labels)

**`ZSDLPIncidentSearchTimeRange`**

| Property | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `startTime` | ZSDLPIncidentDate | no |
| `endTime` | ZSDLPIncidentDate | no |

- `ZSDLPIncidentDate`: string(date-time)

**`Cursor`**

| Property | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `totalPages` | integer | yes |
| `currentPageNumber` | integer | yes |
| `currentPageSize` | integer | yes |
| `pageId` | string | yes |
| `totalElements` | integer | no |

| Property | Type | Required |

**Servers:** `https://{host}:{port}/wapi/v1`, `https://{host}:{port}/api/v1`

### `GET /auth`

Checks if there is an authenticated session.

- Operation ID: `AuthSessionZResource_getAuthenticatedSession`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation. When an authenticated session exists, the response contains authType information. If authType is not present, the authenticated session has expired or does not exist. |

### `POST /auth`

Creates an authenticated session. The response returns a cookie in the header called

`JSESSIONID`

that must be used in subsequent requests.

- Operation ID: `AuthSessionZResource_addAuthenticatedSession`

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |

### `DELETE /auth`

Log out of authenticated session.

- Operation ID: `AuthSessionZResource_deleteAuthenticatedSession`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | default response. See [API Response Codes](https://help.zscaler.com/cloud-branch-connector/api-response-codes-and-error-messages) |

### `GET /cloudApplicationInstances`

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |

### `GET /cloudApplications/policy`

Retrieves a list of Predefined and User Defined Cloud Applications associated with the DLP rules, Cloud App Control rules, Advanced Settings, Bandwidth Classes, and File Type Control rules.

Retrieves AppInfo when groupResults is set to false and retrieves the application count grouped by application category when groupResults is set to true.

- Operation ID: `CloudApplicationsResource_getPolicyWebApplications`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | query | no | object | Filter application by name |
| `pageSize` | query | no | object | Set the size of response |
| `page` | query | no | object | Set the page number of response |
| `appClass` | query | no | object | Filter application by application category |
| `groupResults` | query | no | object | Show count of applications grouped by application category |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

Retrives AppInfo when groupResults is set to false and retrieves the application count grouped by application category when groupResults is set to true.

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | query | no | object | Filter application by name |
| `pageSize` | query | no | object | Set the size of response |
| `page` | query | no | object | Set the page number of response |
| `appClass` | query | no | object | Filter application by application category |
| `groupResults` | query | no | object | Show count of applications grouped by application category |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

To access detailed ZPA API documentation, including references and use cases, refer to the [Zscaler Help Portal](/zpa/about-zpa-api).

### `GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/cloudConnectorGroup/summary`

Gets a summary of Cloud Connector groups for the specified customer.

- Operation ID: `getAllEdgeConnectorGroupNameIds`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customerId` | path | yes | integer(int64) | The unique identifier of the ZPA tenant. |
| `search` | query | no | string | The search string used to support search by features and fields for the API. |
| `page` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page number. |
| `pagesize` | query | no | integer(int32) | Specifies the page size. If not provided, the default page size is 20. The max page size is 500. |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | OK |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed |
| 409 | Conflict |
| 415 | Unsupported Media Type |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |
| 503 | Service Unavailable |

## Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS)

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/cloud-nanolog-streaming-service-nss
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZIA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Reference Guide > Cloud Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS)
- Last modified: 2026-08-09T07:06Z

API Reference Guide for the ZIA Cloud Service and Sandbox Submission APIs

### `GET /nssCollectors`

Retrieves a list of all configured NSS Collector servers. To learn more, see

[About NSS Collector Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-nss-collector-servers)

.

- Operation ID: `NssCollectorResource_getNssCollectors`

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /nssCollectors`

Adds a new NSS Collector server. To learn more, see

[Adding NSS Collector Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-nss-collector-servers)

.

- Operation ID: `NssCollectorResource_createNssCollector`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | body | no | NssCollectorResponse | Information about the NSS Collector server |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `PUT /nssCollectors/{id}`

Updates the NSS Collector server based on the specified ID

- Operation ID: `NssCollectorResource_updateNssCollector`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | body | no | NssCollectorResponse | Information about the NSS Collector server |
| `id` | path | yes | object | System-generated ID for the NSS Collector server |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `DELETE /nssCollectors/{id}`

Deletes the NSS Collector server based on the specified ID

- Operation ID: `NssCollectorResource_deleteRules`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | path | yes | object | System-generated ID for the NSS Collector server |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Successful Operation |

### `GET /nssDownload/{nssId}`

Downloads the NSS server virtual appliance information based on the specified NSS server ID in a .ova format. To learn more, see

[About NSS Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-nss-servers)

.

- Operation ID: `NssDownloadResource_downloadNssCert`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nssId` | path | yes | object | Specifies the NSS server ID |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Successful Operation |

Retrieves a list of registered NSS servers. To learn more, see

[About NSS Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-nss-servers)

.

- Operation ID: `NssResource_getNssServers`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | query | no | object | The server type |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 500 | Internal Server Error |

[Adding NSS Servers](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-nss-servers)

.

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |

| 500 | Internal Server Error |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| --- | --- |

### `PUT /nssFeeds/{feedId}`

Updates cloud NSS feed configuration based on the specified ID. To learn more, see

[Adding Cloud NSS Feeds](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-cloud-nss-feeds)

.

- Operation ID: `NssFeedsResource_updateNssFeed`

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `DELETE /nssFeeds/{feedId}`

Deletes cloud NSS feed configuration based on the specified ID

- Operation ID: `NssFeedsResource_deleteNssFeed`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onPremNss` | query | no | object | A Boolean value indicating whether the feed is on-premises NSS feed |
| `feedId` | path | yes | object | Unique identifier for the cloud NSS feed |
| `cloudNss` | query | no | object | A Boolean value indicating whether the feed is cloud NSS feed |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Successful Operation |

### `GET /nssFeeds/feedOutputDefaults`

Retrieves the default cloud NSS feed output format for different log types

- Operation ID: `NssFeedsResource_getFeedOutPutFormats`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | query | no | object | The type of logs that you are streaming |
| `multiFeedType` | query | no | object | This field is used to set the multi-feed type to Tunnel |
| `fieldFormat` | query | no | object | The feed output type of your SIEM |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `GET /nssFeeds/testConnectivity/{feedId}`

Tests the connectivity of cloud NSS feed based on the specified ID

- Operation ID: `NssFeedsResource_testCloudNssConnectivity`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `feedId` | path | yes | object | Unique identifier for the cloud NSS feed |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

### `POST /nssFeeds/validateFeedFormat`

Validates the cloud NSS feed format and returns the validation result

- Operation ID: `NssFeedsResource_validateFeedFormat`

**Parameters:**

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | query | no | object | The cloud NSS log type |

**Responses:**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | Successful Operation |

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/legacy-apis/configuring-access-policies-using-api","lastmod":"2026-06-10T15:36Z","nid":"1484771"} -->
## Configuring Access Policies Using API

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/legacy-apis/configuring-access-policies-using-api
- Product: Legacy Zscaler APIs
- Path: Legacy Zscaler APIs Help > ZPA API > API Developer & Reference Guide > Working with APIs > Configuring Access Policies Using API
- Last modified: 2026-06-10T15:36Z
- Summary: Information on access policy use cases applicable to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) cloud service API.

This article provides information on managing Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) access policy use cases using APIs. All APIs are rate limited. To learn more, see [Understanding Rate Limiting](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/understanding-rate-limiting).

## Prerequisite API Call

To get the `policySetId` by policy type:

1. Send a `GET` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policySet/policyType/{policyType}`.
2. Provide the `policyType`, the value for differentiating the policy types, in the request endpoint. The supported values are:
  - `ACCESS_POLICY` or `GLOBAL_POLICY` (i.e., access policy)
  - `TIMEOUT_POLICY` or `REAUTH_POLICY` (i.e., timeout policy)
  - `BYPASS_POLICY` or `CLIENT_FORWARDING_POLICY` (i.e., client forwarding policy)
  - `INSPECTION_POLICY` (i.e., AppProtection policy)
  - `ISOLATION_POLICY` (i.e., Isolation policy)
  - `REDIRECTION_POLICY` (i.e., redirection policy)
  - `CAPABILITIES_POLICY` (i.e., privileged capabilities policy)
  - `CREDENTIAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged credential policy)
  - `CLIENTLESS_SESSION_PROTECTION_POLICY` (i.e., Browser Protection policy)
  - `PRIVILEGED_PORTAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged portal policy)

For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/217246660302995456/policySet/policyType/ACCESS_POLICY`.

- View an example response

```
{
"id":"217246660303020009",
"modifiedTime":"1627689868",
"creationTime":"1480979629",
"modifiedBy":"217246660303025242",
"name":"Global_Policy",
"enabled":true,
"description":"The rules in this policy set are executed first.",
"policyType":"1"
}
```

A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

This API supports pagination. To get a paginated response:

1. Send a `GET` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policySet/rules/policyType/{policyType}?page=1&pagesize=20`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint:

- `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
- `policyType`: The value for differentiating the policy types. The supported values are:
  - `ACCESS_POLICY` or `GLOBAL_POLICY` (i.e., access policy)
  - `TIMEOUT_POLICY` or `REAUTH_POLICY` (i.e., timeout policy)
  - `BYPASS_POLICY` or `CLIENT_FORWARDING_POLICY` (i.e., client forwarding policy)
  - `INSPECTION_POLICY` (i.e., AppProtection policy)
  - `ISOLATION_POLICY` (i.e., Isolation policy)
  - `REDIRECTION_POLICY` (i.e., redirection policy)
  - `CAPABILITIES_POLICY` (i.e., privileged capabilities policy)
  - `CREDENTIAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged credential policy)
  - `CLIENTLESS_SESSION_PROTECTION_POLICY` (i.e., Browser Protection policy)
  - `PRIVILEGED_PORTAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged portal policy)
- Valid values for page and page size parameters.

For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/217246660302995456/policySet/rules/policyType/ACCESS_POLICY?page=1&pagesize=2.`

- View an example response

```
{
"totalPages":"16",
"list":[
{

If not provided, the default page size is 20. The maximum page size is 500.

A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

This API supports a search option to get rules by action. To search by features and fields:

1. Send a GET request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policySet/rules/policyType/{policyType}?page=1&pagesize=20&search={searchString}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/72057594037927936/policySet/rules/policyType/ACCESS_POLICY?page=1&pagesize=500&search=action%20EQ%20ALLOW`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `policyType`: The value for differentiating the policy types. The supported values are:
    - `ACCESS_POLICY` or `GLOBAL_POLICY` (i.e., access policy)
    - `TIMEOUT_POLICY` or `REAUTH_POLICY` (i.e., timeout policy)
    - `BYPASS_POLICY` or `CLIENT_FORWARDING_POLICY` (i.e., client forwarding policy)
    - `INSPECTION_POLICY` (i.e., AppProtection policy)
    - `ISOLATION_POLICY` (i.e., Isolation policy)
    - `REDIRECTION_POLICY` (i.e., redirection policy)
    - `CAPABILITIES_POLICY` (i.e., privileged capabilities policy)
    - `CREDENTIAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged credential policy)
    - `CLIENTLESS_SESSION_PROTECTION_POLICY` (i.e., Browser Protection policy)
    - `PRIVILEGED_PORTAL_POLICY` (i.e., privileged portal policy)
  - Valid page and page size values.
  - Valid search string values. The search string values are in the format `action OPERATOR ruleAction`. The supported `ruleAction` values for access policies are `ALLOW` and `DENY`. The supported value for `OPERATOR` is `EQ` (i.e., equals). Only search string values that correspond to the values for valid rule actions and operators are supported. For example, the string `action%20EQ%ALLOW` is supported for the **Rule Action** filter, using the **Equals** operator, for the `ALLOW` rule action.

If not provided, the default page size is 20. The maximum page size is 500.

- View an example response

      }

```

A successful response returns code 200. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

### Getting the Required Policy Criteria Details

Before creating a new access policy rule, you must get the following required details for the policy criteria:

- Application Segment. To learn more, see [Configuring Application Segments Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-application-segments-using-api#getAppSegments).
- Client types. To learn more, see Getting Details of All Client Types.
- Cloud Connector Group. To learn more, see [Obtaining Cloud Connector Group Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-cloud-connector-group-details-using-api).
- IdP. To learn more, see [Obtaining IdP Configuration Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-idp-configuration-details-using-api).
- Machine Group. To learn more, see [Obtaining Machine Group Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-machine-group-details-using-api).
- Platform types. To learn more, see Getting Platform Types for a Customer.
- Posture profile. To learn more, see [Obtaining Posture Profile Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-posture-profile-details-using-api).
- SAML attribute. To learn more, see [Obtaining SAML Attribute Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-saml-attribute-details-using-api).
- Segment Group. To learn more, see [Configuring Segment Groups Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-segment-groups-using-api#getSegmentGroups).
- SCIM attribute. To learn more, see [Obtaining SCIM Attribute Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-scim-attribute-details-using-api).
- SCIM attribute value. To learn more, see [Obtaining SCIM Attribute Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-scim-attribute-details-using-api#getSCIMvalue).
- SCIM Group. To learn more, see [Obtaining SCIM Group Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-scim-group-details-using-api).
- Trusted network. To learn more, see [Obtaining Trusted Network Details Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/obtaining-trusted-network-details-using-api).

## Creating a New Access Policy Rule

To add a new access policy rule for a given policy set and for a given `customerId`:

1. Send a `POST` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/{customerId}/policySet/{policySetId}/rule`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint: For example: `/mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/217316918451765248/policySet/217316918451765253/rule`.
  - `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
  - `policySetId`: The ID of the global policy set captured in Prerequisite API Call.
3. Include the request headers to specify the following parameters about the request context:
  - Content-Type: `application/json`
  - Authorization: `Bearer <access_token>`
4. Use the entire JSON payload and provide the policy criteria you want for the criteria.

- View the JSON payload

```
{
    "policySetId": "<policySetId>",
    "conditions": [
        {
            "operands": [
                {
                    "objectType": "APP",
                    "values": [
                        "<applicationId>",
                        "<applicationId>",
                        "<applicationId>"
                    ]
                },
                {
                    "objectType": "APP_GROUP",
                    "values": [
                        "<segmentGroupId>"
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
    "name": "<Example Policy Rule Name>",
    "description": "<Example Policy Rule Description>",
    "action": "ALLOW",
    "appConnectorGroups": [
        {
            "id": "<appConnectorGroupId>",
            "name": "<Example App Connector Group Name>"
        },
        {
            "id": "<appConnectorGroupId>",
            "name": "<Example App Connector Group Name 2>"
        }
    ],
    "appServerGroups": [],
    "customMsg": "MsgString"
}
```

- View an example response

```
{
  "id":"72057615512764594",
  "creationTime":"1612289724",
  "modifiedBy":"72057615512764593",
  "name":"PolicyName",
  "description":"Description",
  "ruleOrder":"5",
  "priority":"1",
  "policyType":"1",
  "operator":"AND",
  "action":"ALLOW",
  "customMsg":"MsgString",
  "auditMessage":"string"
}
```

A successful response returns code 201. To learn more, see [API Response Codes and Error Messages](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/api-response-codes-and-error-messages).

### Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Support

To create an access policy rule with a required approval:

1. Send a `POST` request to the following endpoint: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policySet/{policySetId}/rule?microtenantId={microtenantId}`.
2. Provide the following in the request endpoint:

- `customerId`: The ZPA tenant ID of the customer.
- `policySetId`: The ID of the global policy set captured in the Prerequisite API Call section.
- `microtenantId`: The unique identifier of the Microtenant for the ZPA tenant. To learn more, see [Configuring Microtenants Using API](https://help.zscaler.com/zpa/configuring-microtenants-using-api).

For example: `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/289370814522851328/policySet/289370814522851333/rule?microtenantId=145260601092866314`.

1. Include the request headers to specify the following parameters about the request context:

- Content-Type: `application/json`
- Authorization: `Bearer <access_token>`

1. Use the following JSON payload and provide the following:

- Ensure `action` is set to `REQUIRE_APPROVAL`
- The policy criteria you want to include.
